physics-h2-q2.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.

physics-killer-11.title: Photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality of light and microscopic world
physics-killer-11.topic: Photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality of light and microscopic world
physics-killer-11.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-11.material: Particle P enter perpendicular to uniform magnetic field $B$ and do uniform circular motion, with orbit radius $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and period $2\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Particle Q enter perpendicular to di same magnetic field as P, and im mass na $4$ times dat of P, di size of im charge na $2$ times dat of P, and im speed na $3$ times dat of P. Ignore gravity. Which one correctly match, in order, di orbit radius and period of Q?
physics-killer-11.thinking.0: Photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality of light and microscopic world
physics-killer-11.s.s1.prompt: Particle P enter perpendicular to uniform magnetic field $B$ and do uniform circular motion, with orbit radius $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and period $2\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Particle Q enter perpendicular to di same magnetic field as P, and im mass na $4$ times dat of P, di size of im charge na $2$ times dat of P, and im speed na $3$ times dat of P. Ignore gravity. Which one correctly match, in order, di orbit radius and period of Q?
physics-killer-11.s.s1.explain: Because $r\propto\dfrac{mv}{q}$, $\dfrac{r_Q}{r_P}=\dfrac{4m\cdot3v}{2q}\cdot\dfrac{q}{mv}=6\Rightarrow r_Q=5\times6=30\,\mathrm{cm}$. Because $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ no depend on speed, $\dfrac{T_Q}{T_P}=\dfrac{4}{2}=2\Rightarrow T_Q=4\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. If you forget di charge ratio e be $r=60\,\mathrm{cm}$, $T=8\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ (wrong answer ①), if you think di period dey proportional to speed e be $12\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ (wrong answer ③), and if you ignore both mass and charge ratio and use only di speed ratio e be $r=15\,\mathrm{cm}$ (wrong answer ④).
physics-killer-11.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-killer-11.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
physics-killer-11.s.s1.hint.0: From $qvB=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$ e be $r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$, period $T=\dfrac{2\pi r}{v}=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ (no depend on speed).
